question.problem: The axis of symmetry of $y=\frac{1}{3}(k-x)(5x+3k)$ is $x=\frac{1}{10}.$ The value of $k=$
question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{10},$ we will set our result equal to $\frac{1}{10}.$ 

From the equation $y=\frac{1}{3}(k-x)(5x+3k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are ${x}_{1}=k$ and ${x}_{2}=-\frac{3k}{5}.$ 

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{(k-\frac{3k}{5})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{5k}{5}-\frac{3k}{5})}{2} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{2k}{5})}{2} \\  & =\frac{k}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\frac{1}{10}.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{k}{5} & =\frac{1}{10} \\ k & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
